user.title: Connect to your S3 bucket
user.description: Point this integration at an S3 or S3-compatible bucket, choose the folder it is allowed to touch, and switch on the actions you want. Everything except the folder can be changed later from the integration's Configure button.

data.root_prefix: Folder this integration is limited to

data_description.bucket: The bucket name, for example ha-files. It must already exist.
data_description.endpoint_url: For S3-compatible servers such as MinIO, Ceph or Backblaze B2, for example https://minio.local:9000. Leave empty for Amazon S3.
data_description.region: Amazon S3 needs the bucket's real region. Almost every S3-compatible server accepts us-east-1.
data_description.access_key_id: Leave both key fields empty to use credentials from the environment, such as an instance role.
data_description.secret_access_key: Stored in Home Assistant's config entry and never written to diagnostics. Leave it blank later to keep the secret you already have.
data_description.path_style: Required by most S3-compatible servers. Turn this off to use virtual-hosted style addressing on Amazon S3.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only for a server with a self-signed certificate.
data_description.root_prefix: The only folder this integration can reach, for example homeassistant/notes. Every path the assistant sees and returns is relative to this folder. Leave empty to allow the whole bucket.
data_description.notes_folder: Where 'take a note' saves new notes, relative to the folder above. Leave this empty to save notes directly in that folder.
data_description.show_file_details: Whether the sidebar shows each file's extension, its size and its date. Turn this off for a plain list of names.
data_description.max_results: The most entries one listing may return. Keeps a large bucket from flooding an assistant's context.
data_description.max_read_bytes: The largest file that may be read into an assistant's context. Larger files are truncated and flagged.
data_description.allow_list: Adds the list_files action. Without it nothing can discover paths, so read, move and delete become hard to use.
data_description.allow_write: Adds the write_file and 'take a note' actions, both of which create or replace objects.
data_description.allow_delete: Adds the delete_file action. Deleting an S3 object cannot be undone.
data_description.allow_move: Adds the move_file action. A move copies the object and then deletes the original.
data_description.allow_mkdir: Adds the create_folder action. S3 has no real folders, so this writes an empty folder marker that makes an otherwise empty folder visible.

error.invalid_root_prefix: That folder is not valid. It must not contain '..' segments.
error.invalid_notes_folder: That notes folder is not valid. It must not contain '..' segments.
error.credentials_incomplete: Fill in both the access key ID and the secret access key, or leave both empty.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the endpoint. Check the URL, and that Home Assistant can reach it.
error.bucket_not_found: The endpoint does not have a bucket with that name.
error.unknown: Something went wrong talking to the endpoint. Check the Home Assistant log for the details.

abort.already_configured: S3 Files is already set up. Use the Configure button on the integration to change its settings.
